criteria.name: Clock
criteria.answer: A clock is a self-driven part with a reading that ticks; uniform ring clocks are classified; a reading resets the clock, frequent reading stops it, and the cost spread limits the resolution.

criteria.name: Time and λ
criteria.answer: In a state without λ-dependence the rest evolves by its own contract, indexed by the clock reading; rates per λ are rates per clock time with factor one, within the clock's bandwidth and for suitable contracts between clock and rest.

criteria.name: Comparison of clocks
criteria.answer: Free clocks are compared by the ratio of their ticks; one joint reading synchronizes identical clocks up to the recorded offset; in an environment a clock stays uniform iff it is coupled through its own contract, and two clocks keep their rate ratio iff the coupling strengths are equal.

criteria.name: Proper time and moving clocks
criteria.answer: For Model D bodies a carried clock slows down with the drift speed V, tick ratio 1 + V²/(2 v_max²) at small speed; its time along a path is the integral of √(1 − V²/v_max²) up to lattice corrections; between two meetings the resting clock shows more; a clock that commutes with the motion is not affected.

criteria.name: Inertia and internal energy
criteria.answer: For Model D bodies the averaged inertia is half the gap between the branches divided by v_max², and the clock's cost adds to it like the rest term; the inverse inertia of 03-ilang-space vanishes for the same body; for a clock that commutes with the motion the inertia does not depend on the clock.

criteria.name: Common maximal speed
criteria.answer: No: the maximal speed belongs to a type, and the laws do not make it equal for two types; equality is a condition on the description, equivalent to a common leading-order slowdown law and a common relation between inertia and rest gap.

criteria.name: Events and causal order
criteria.answer: Readings are events; a reading can influence only readings at larger λ; the influence at distance r starts at order δ^r in the delay and obeys a bound with a finite speed, but there is no sharp cone, so the order is only approximate; whether a generic chain of three or more cells has influence at every delay is undecided.

criteria.name: Global order
criteria.answer: With respect to linear re-timings of two parts: the unit of λ is never detectable; its direction is detectable wherever one reading can influence another, and is fixed by the reading rule; a common now is not detectable for uncoupled parts, and for coupled parts it is detectable iff the contract has no split into commuting pieces that each leave the places of one part unchanged; on a chain the order of two events leaves a trace in the statistics iff one can influence the other.
